newsitem.title: USA: Texaco begins Captain Field production.
newsitem.headline: Texaco begins Captain Field production.

text.p: Texaco Inc said the Capitan Field in the British North Sea, about 90 miles northeast of Aberdeen, produced its first oil Thursday.
The company had hoped to begin production in December, but was delayed by weather, spokesman Jim Swords said.
The company said the initial production phase will be followed by continued field development in preparation for peak production from the field, expected to be 63,000 barrels per day, by mid-1997.
This target is unchanged, Swords said.

Calling the Captain field a major development for Texaco, the company said it developed the project as the 100 percent owner and operator. However, as previously announced, the Korea Captain Co Ltd, a consortium of Korea Petroleum Development Corp and Hanwha Energy, has agreed in principle to acquire a 15-percent interest.

The $800 million project used advanced technology to fast-track the field's development. To get maximum extraction from the reservoir, Texaco has employed a unique combination of horizontal drilling, electrical submersible pumps, and floating production, storage and off-loading vessel technology.
The field infrastructure comprises a wellhead protector platform connected by a network of pipelines to the vessel, where the crude oil is processed and stored.
Oil from the field is exported by shuttle tanker, either directly to customers or to the Nigg Bay terminal in the Cromarty Firth.
